Development Guide: Adding Functions to WJPr

Source: vignettes/articles/development-guide.Rmd
development-guide.Rmd

This technical guide walks through the complete process for adding new visualization functions to the WJPr package.

Prerequisites

Development Dependencies 

install.packages(c(
  "devtools",
  "roxygen2",
  "testthat",
  "usethis",
  "pkgdown"
))

Clone the Repository 

git clone https://github.com/worldjusticeproject/WJPr.git
cd WJPr

Then restore the project environment with renv::restore().

Step 1: Create the Function File

Location and Naming

Create a new file in R/ following the convention:

  • Charts: {type}Chart.R (e.g., waterfallChart.R)
  • Utilities: {name}.R (e.g., validation.R)
# Create the file
usethis::use_r("waterfallChart")

Step 2: Function Structure

Complete Template 

#' Plot a Waterfall Chart following WJP style guidelines
#'
#' @description
#' `r lifecycle::badge("experimental")`
#'
#' `wjp_waterfall()` creates a waterfall chart showing the cumulative effect
#' of sequential positive and negative values.
#'
#' @param data Data frame containing the data to plot.
#' @param target String. Column name with numeric values to plot.
#' @param grouping String. Column name with category labels.
#' @param colors String. Column name for color grouping. Default is `NULL`.
#' @param cvec Named vector of colors. Default is `NULL` (the WJP palette,
#'   see [wjp_palette()], is applied).
#' @param labels String. Column name with value labels. Default is `NULL`.
#' @param direction String. `"horizontal"` or `"vertical"`. Default is `"vertical"`.
#' @param ptheme ggplot theme to apply. Default is [WJP_theme()].
#' @param show_legend Logical. If `TRUE`, displays a horizontal legend above
#'   the chart. Default is `FALSE`.
#'
#' @return A ggplot object representing the waterfall chart.
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' # Always load the WJP fonts
#' wjp_fonts()
#'
#' # Prepare data
#' data_waterfall <- data.frame(
#'   category = c("Start", "Gain A", "Loss B", "Gain C", "End"),
#'   value    = c(100, 30, -20, 15, 125),
#'   type     = c("total", "positive", "negative", "positive", "total")
#' )
#'
#' # Create chart
#' wjp_waterfall(
#'   data_waterfall,
#'   target   = "value",
#'   grouping = "category",
#'   colors   = "type",
#'   cvec     = c("total"    = "#482d8b",
#'                "positive" = "#0f9581",
#'                "negative" = "#f26b21")
#' )

wjp_waterfall <- function(
    data,
    target,
    grouping,
    colors      = NULL,
    cvec        = NULL,
    labels      = NULL,
    direction   = "vertical",
    ptheme      = WJP_theme(),
    show_legend = FALSE
) {

  # ===========================================================================
  # SECTION 1: INPUT VALIDATION (optional but recommended)
  # ===========================================================================

  if (!is.data.frame(data)) {
    stop("`data` must be a data frame.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (!target %in% names(data)) {
    stop("Column '", target, "' not found in `data`.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (!direction %in% c("vertical", "horizontal")) {
    stop('`direction` must be one of "vertical" or "horizontal".', call. = FALSE)
  }

  # ===========================================================================
  # SECTION 2: RENAME VARIABLES
  # ===========================================================================

  # Rename the required columns
  data <- data %>%
    dplyr::rename(
      target_var   = dplyr::all_of(target),
      grouping_var = dplyr::all_of(grouping)
    )

  # Handle the colors column
  if (is.null(colors) || identical(colors, grouping)) {
    # If not supplied (or the same column as grouping), reuse grouping
    data <- data %>%
      dplyr::mutate(colors_var = grouping_var)
  } else {
    data <- data %>%
      dplyr::rename(colors_var = dplyr::all_of(colors))
  }

  # Handle labels
  if (is.null(labels)) {
    data <- data %>%
      dplyr::mutate(labels_var = "")
  } else if (identical(labels, grouping)) {
    data <- data %>%
      dplyr::mutate(labels_var = grouping_var)
  } else if (identical(labels, colors)) {
    data <- data %>%
      dplyr::mutate(labels_var = colors_var)
  } else {
    data <- data %>%
      dplyr::rename(labels_var = dplyr::all_of(labels))
  }

  # ===========================================================================
  # SECTION 3: DATA TRANSFORMATIONS
  # ===========================================================================

  # Compute the waterfall positions
  data <- data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      end   = cumsum(target_var),
      start = dplyr::lag(end, default = 0),
      # Handle negative values
      ymin  = pmin(start, end),
      ymax  = pmax(start, end)
    )

  # ===========================================================================
  # SECTION 4: DEFAULT COLORS
  # ===========================================================================

  # Fall back to the WJP palette when no color vector is supplied
  if (is.null(cvec)) {
    cvec <- wjp_default_cvec(data$colors_var)
  }

  # ===========================================================================
  # SECTION 5: BASE CHART
  # ===========================================================================

  plt <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    data,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x    = grouping_var,
      fill = colors_var
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_rect(
      ggplot2::aes(
        xmin = as.numeric(factor(grouping_var)) - 0.4,
        xmax = as.numeric(factor(grouping_var)) + 0.4,
        ymin = ymin,
        ymax = ymax
      ),
      show.legend = show_legend
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
      values = cvec,
      breaks = wjp_legend_breaks(data$colors_var),
      name   = NULL
    )

  # Add value labels if supplied
  if (!all(data$labels_var == "")) {
    plt <- plt +
      ggplot2::geom_text(
        ggplot2::aes(
          x     = grouping_var,
          y     = ymax,
          label = labels_var
        ),
        vjust    = -0.5,
        family   = wjp_font_family(),
        fontface = "bold",
        size     = 3.514598,
        color    = "#4a4a49"
      )
  }

  # ===========================================================================
  # SECTION 6: DIRECTION
  # ===========================================================================

  if (direction == "horizontal") {
    plt <- plt +
      ggplot2::coord_flip()
  }

  # ===========================================================================
  # SECTION 7: THEME AND FINAL TWEAKS
  # ===========================================================================

  plt <- plt +
    ptheme +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "", y = "") +
    ggplot2::theme(
      panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank()
    ) +
    wjp_legend_theme(show_legend)

  return(plt)
}

Step 3: Important Patterns

Handling Optional Parameters

The most important pattern is handling a parameter that is NULL or two parameters that point to the same column:

# INCORRECT - Fails if colors == grouping
data <- data %>%
  rename(
    grouping_var = all_of(grouping),
    colors_var   = all_of(colors)  # ERROR: column already renamed
  )

# CORRECT - Check before renaming
if (is.null(colors) || identical(colors, grouping)) {
  data <- data %>%
    mutate(colors_var = grouping_var)
} else {
  data <- data %>%
    rename(colors_var = all_of(colors))
}

Named Color Vector 

# Names must match the values of the colors variable EXACTLY
cvec <- c(
  "Trust"    = "#482d8b",
  "No Trust" = "#f26b21"
)

# Inside the function, fall back to the WJP palette when cvec is NULL
if (is.null(cvec)) {
  cvec <- wjp_default_cvec(data$colors_var)
}
plt <- plt +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cvec)

Fonts

Never hard-code a font family. Read the active one with wjp_font_family() so options(wjpr.family = "Inter Tight") switches every chart:

geom_text(
  family   = wjp_font_family(),
  fontface = "bold",
  size     = 3.514598  # 10 pt value labels
)

Polar Coordinates (Circular Charts)

For radar, rose, or gauge charts:

plt <- plt +
  coord_polar(
    theta = "y",      # Variable mapped to the angle
    start = pi        # Starting point (pi = bottom)
  ) +
  theme(
    aspect.ratio = 1  # Keep a 1:1 ratio for a circle
  )

Invisible Segments

To control the visual range without affecting the data (as wjp_gauge() does to draw a semicircle):

# Add a transparent padding segment
padding_data <- data.frame(
  colors_var = "___padding___",
  target_var = 50
)

data <- dplyr::bind_rows(data, padding_data)
cvec <- c(cvec, "___padding___" = "transparent")

Keep technical segments out of the legend by passing the visible categories as breaks (see wjp_legend_breaks()).

Deprecating Parameters

When a parameter is renamed, keep the old name working and signal the change:

wjp_waterfall <- function(data, target, grouping, order = NULL, order_var = deprecated()) {
  if (lifecycle::is_present(order_var)) {
    lifecycle::deprecate_soft("1.2.0", "wjp_waterfall(order_var)", "wjp_waterfall(order)")
    if (is.null(order)) order <- order_var
  }
  ...
}

Step 4: Roxygen2 Documentation

Required Tags

Tag Description Example
@description Detailed description Include the lifecycle badge
@param Every parameter @param data Data frame containing...
@return Returned value @return A ggplot object
@export Export the function Always include
@examples Reproducible example Runnable code

Lifecycle Badge

Always include the function status:

#' @description
#' `r lifecycle::badge("experimental")`
#'
#' Description of the function...

Options: - "experimental" - New, may change - "stable" - Stable API - "deprecated" - Do not use, will be removed

Step 5: Add Tests

Create or extend a file in tests/testthat/:

test_that("wjp_waterfall returns a buildable ggplot", {
  data <- data.frame(
    category = c("Start", "Gain", "Loss"),
    value    = c(100, 30, -20)
  )

  plot <- wjp_waterfall(data, target = "value", grouping = "category")

  expect_s3_class(plot, "ggplot")
  expect_no_error(ggplot2::ggplot_build(plot))
})

Step 6: Add a Visual Example

Update generate-examples.R

Add a section to data-raw/generate-examples.R:

# =============================================================================
# XX. WATERFALL CHART
# =============================================================================
message("XX. Generating waterfall chart example...")

data_waterfall <- data.frame(
  category = c("Start", "Revenue", "Costs", "Taxes", "End"),
  value    = c(100, 50, -30, -10, 110),
  type     = c("total", "gain", "loss", "loss", "total")
)

plot_waterfall <- wjp_waterfall(
  data_waterfall,
  target   = "value",
  grouping = "category",
  colors   = "type",
  cvec     = c("total" = "#482d8b",
               "gain"  = "#0f9581",
               "loss"  = "#f26b21")
)

save_example(plot_waterfall, "waterfall")

Generate the Image 

source("data-raw/generate-examples.R")

Step 7: Register the Function

  • Add the function to _pkgdown.yml (the functions navbar menu and the reference index).
  • Add a section to vignettes/articles/gallery.Rmd.
  • Add an entry to NEWS.md.
  • Add the function to the chart table in CLAUDE.md:
| `wjp_waterfall()` | waterfallChart.R | Waterfall chart for cumulative changes |

Step 8: Verification

Pre-PR Checklist 

# 1. Regenerate documentation
devtools::document()

# 2. Run the tests
devtools::test()

# 3. Check the package
devtools::check()

# 4. Load and try it
devtools::load_all()
wjp_fonts()
# ... example code

# 5. Generate the image
source("data-raw/generate-examples.R")

Common Errors

Error Cause Solution
object 'x' not found Variable not renamed Check the rename step
Column doesn't exist Double rename Use if/else to avoid it
NULL result Missing return() Add return(plt)
Font not found Fonts not loaded Call wjp_fonts()
no visible binding for global variable (check NOTE) Column used in aes()/mutate() Add it to globalVariables() in R/WJPr-package.R

Step 9: Pull Request

Create a Branch 

git checkout -b feature/waterfall-chart

Commit 

git add R/waterfallChart.R
git add man/wjp_waterfall.Rd
git add man/figures/example-waterfall.png
git add tests/testthat/test-charts.R
git add data-raw/generate-examples.R
git add _pkgdown.yml NEWS.md CLAUDE.md

git commit -m "Add wjp_waterfall() chart function

- New waterfall chart for cumulative changes
- Supports horizontal/vertical direction
- Full Roxygen2 documentation and tests
- Example image generated"

Push and PR 

git push origin feature/waterfall-chart

Open a PR on GitHub with: - A description of the function - A screenshot of the chart - The completed checklist
